records.verificationNote: Read CDL pp.7, 110, 125-126. Judgment on Code I: CDL General Provision 2 (p.4) says starred drugs need authorization unless used under the conditions the CDL specifies. This record treats the controlled-substance policy (p.7) as those conditions, so zolpidem is covered within those limits. If Medi-Cal Rx reads starred entries as PA-required, zolpidem moves to paRequired. The CDL also states DHCS recommends hypnotic use be 'occasional rather than continuous' (p.126); recorded here, not as a step. Zolpidem chosen as the standard Z-drug (judgment). Doxepin capsules listed are antidepressant strengths, not Silenor. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: CDL p.4 General Provision 2: "Code I drugs marked with a symbol (*) require authorization in accordance with Section 51003 unless used under the conditions specified in the Contract Drugs List". For zolpidem (p.126) and hydrocodone/APAP (p.94) the printed Code I condition is "Refer to the Controlled Substance Policy section for drug-specific limitations" (p.7), so the star is a use limit, not a PA; contrast meperidine elixir, which prints "requires a PA" (p.94). Pick kept; verification stays partial (starred wording is ambiguous on its face). Unlisted-product rows quote p.4: "Legend drugs not listed may be covered subject to authorization from a Medi-Cal consultant." Confirmed by text search of the full CDL: none of eszopiclone, zaleplon, tapentadol appear.]

records.verificationNote: Preferred: zolpidem tartrate tabs 5 mg (PDF p.55, Tier 1, QL - 30 day(s)). Only zolpidem 5 mg is printed (no 10 mg tablet line). The QL (30 days) is the printed quantity limit; no PA or step flag. Not printed: eszopiclone (Lunesta), zaleplon, Ambien CR, Edluar; treated as unconfirmed. Ramelteon 8 mg (PDF p.55) and doxepin 3/6 mg tabs (PDF p.54) are printed and listed as alternatives per the class description. Document says: "Kaiser Foundation Health Plan does not have a requirement for PA" (PDF p.6) and "does not have a requirement for Step Therapy" (PDF p.7). Drugs not listed are nonformulary; when a Kaiser or referral doctor determines one is medically appropriate and necessary it is covered by formulary exception (PDF p.7; decision within 72 hours, 24 urgent, PDF p.8). Completeness is ambiguous: p.6 defines the formulary as "the complete list of prescription drugs preferred for use and eligible for coverage" but p.2 says "not an all-inclusive list", so absence is not treated as exclusion. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: pick, tier and flags re-read in the document; 4 named absent drug(s) added as nonformulary (exception route)]
